decision: Preserve default gameplay. No direction policy beat the original aim on validation; the tie-break selected legacy. No changed policy advanced to a complete-period strength comparison.

learning.method: Ridge logistic regression, fixed ridge 10, equal total weight per case.
learning.target: Goal during bounded attack, including friendly rebounds; not calibrated game-wide xG.
learning.selection: Validation attack goals minus goals conceded; ties choose fewer overrides, with legacy first.

audit.native_check_scope: Nine pads, both net ends, both handedness values.

selected_legacy_full_period_parity.purpose: Runtime plumbing verification only; both arms implement the original aim.

limitations: First normal-shot starts per baseline period, collected before outcomes.
Nine screen-direction inputs; four-frame C hold and original follow-through side.
Every baseline fork equals the unmodified controller; first control repeated per period.
Only original aim changes; subsequent shots/passes use Classic.
Primary goal separately attributed; attack goal includes rebounds and subsequent finishes.
Attack ends at goal, four opponent-ownership or stopped-clock frames, period end, or horizon.
Overlapping cases are correlated; split complete seeds and both assignments together.
Training uses seeds 26101–26120; validation uses 26201–26210. The latter chooses the policy and is not a final independent strength test.
Four-frame stable opponent possession ends the attack; shorter possession transients do not.
No attributed original release and unresolved/horizon cases remain in attack-return evaluation; they are not invented primary-shot successes.
Fourteen training and nine validation cases lack complete features. Learned selectors retain legacy aim on those cases, which remain in evaluation.
Height is a raw screen input: UP high, no vertical input middle, DOWN low at both ends. Direction can also affect motion during native execution and cached input after release.
The original horizontal follow-through side, shot trigger and C hold stay fixed. This does not isolate puck height from every movement consequence of the input.
Primary-shot outcomes and later attack finishes are distinct; later finishes can include friendly rebounds and new shots/passes.
Hindsight best-of-nine counts are ceilings on these recorded alternatives, not an executable policy or an unbiased measure of learnable improvement.
Two fixed rosters, first-period states and a bounded horizon do not establish performance against other opponents or across full matches.
A single replay intervention and repeated interventions during gameplay can have different effects.
The earlier 16-case pilot was exploratory and excluded from these totals; its seeds were recollected with the final audited implementation.
No new gameplay flag or default policy change.
